issue_context.title: Problematic predicate pusdown when filtering based on list index.
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.
- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl

lf = pl.LazyFrame({'x' : [1,2,2], 'a' : [[1],[4,3], [5,4]]})

(lf.filter(pl.col('x')==2)
   .filter(pl.col('a').list.get(1).is_in([3]))
   .collect())

# polars.exceptions.ComputeError: get index is out of bounds
```

### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

The error occurs because the second filter is applied first, when the list with length 1 is still present. Using `.collect(predicate_pushdown=False)` or `.list.get(1, null_on_oob=True)` (#16841) gives the expected result.

```python
# shape: (1, 2)
# ┌─────┬───────────┐
# │ x   ┆ a         │
# │ --- ┆ ---       │
# │ i64 ┆ list[i64] │
# ╞═════╪═══════════╡
# │ 2   ┆ [4, 3]    │
# └─────┴───────────┘
```

### Expected behavior

The output should not depend on optimizations.

comments: @nameexhaustion the code in the predicate pushdown checks is mostly yours.  Can you add a case where we move a `list.get (with raise oob)` to local if we add a new filter?

review_comments:
drive-by perf, we only need to check the newly added predicates, currently we check the entire list of predicates at every LP we pass through 🫠.

I seem to remember a while ago someone complained about `collect()` speed regression, maybe this was the cause 😅
